question: The 12 principles of good democratic governance – adopted by the Council of Europe and reaffirmed in Recommendation CM/Rec(2023)5 – aim to enhance transparency, accountability, efficiency and participation at local and regional level.

The debate on the future of the EU’s cohesion policy has shown, also against the backdrop of the report by the High Level Group set up by the Commission, that quality of governance and administrative capacity have a decisive influence on how efficiently EU funds are used, particularly in less developed regions.

In this context, several local governments in the EU have adopted governance quality assurance tools, in line with these principles, in order to help improve administrative performance. In light of the above: 1.
Will the Commission promote the integration of the principles of good governance into post-2027 cohesion policy programmes?
Will it consider introducing reward mechanisms for bodies that adopt recognised standards of good governance?
What steps will it take to strengthen the administrative capacity of local and regional authorities, including through technical support tools and the exchange of good practices?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.7.2026) 1. Addressing the need to enhance administrative capacity remains a top priority under the proposal for a National and Regional Partnership Fund1.

Under Article 3(1)(e)(III) the proposal includes a specific objective on enhancing the efficiency of public administration and the institutional capacity of public authorities and stakeholders at national, regional and local level.

All National and Regional Partnership Plans should contribute to that objective and set out measures to enhance the quality of governance and reinforce the administrative capacity of public administrations. 2. In addition to investments, the plans will incentivise reforms, including for enhancing the quality of governance to address the identified needs and challenges at national, regional and local level.

The framework for programming and implementing reforms has incentivising effects through payments for fulfilled milestones and targets including for governanceenhancing measures. 3. Member States are encouraged to use their technical assistance from the funds to enhance the administrative capacity of plan authorities, stakeholders and beneficiaries, which is necessary for the effective implementation of the Plan.

The Commission will continue to support EU-wide networks of Member States’ authorities and other relevant stakeholders, including for the purposes of exchanging good practices and promoting good governance.

In addition, Member States can request technical support from the EU Facility under the National and Regional Partnership Fund to prepare reforms at national or sub-national level included in their National and Regional Partnership Plans.
